children: Interarch Building Solutions Ltd on Thursday (September 24) said it has inaugurated a new heavy structural steel manufacturing facility at Attivaram in Andhra Pradesh, with an initial manufacturing capacity of 24,000 MT per annum, expanding its capabilities in complex and heavy steel structures.

The facility has been developed across approximately 20 acres, with Phase I utilising around 25,000 square metres of built-up area. The balance land has been earmarked for the development of Phases 2 and 3, with civil works for Phase 2 currently underway.

The new plant is equipped with specialised and high-precision machinery sourced from technology providers in Europe and India. It is designed to manufacture complex heavy structural members for projects where scale, precision and engineering specifications are critical.

The facility will cater to applications across high-rise buildings, data centres, semiconductor and electronics facilities, renewable energy projects, electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure and large industrial developments.

A key capability of the facility is the fabrication of large-sized hot-rolled sections and plate girder structural members. These components are designed for projects requiring stringent engineering and dimensional specifications.

The new facility also expands Interarch's manufacturing portfolio beyond conventional pre-engineered building (PEB) applications and enables the company to undertake projects requiring sophisticated and heavy structural steel solutions.

Located in Andhra Pradesh, the facility will serve customers across South and West India. Its proximity to industrial clusters, ports and major transportation networks is expected to support the movement of materials and finished structures to project locations.

The new facility complements Interarch's existing manufacturing ecosystem at Attivaram. The company had earlier commissioned Phase 2 of its PEB facility at the location, with an installed capacity of 24,000 MT per annum.

That facility involved an investment of approximately ₹32 crore, making Attivaram an increasingly important manufacturing hub for Interarch's steel construction operations. The new facility marks an expansion of its manufacturing capabilities into heavy structural steel and complex steel structures.

Arvind Nanda, Managing Director, Interarch Building Solutions Ltd, said, "The inauguration of our Attivaram facility marks a significant milestone in Interarch’s evolution as a comprehensive steel construction solutions provider.

India is entering a phase of accelerated industrial and infrastructure development, creating demand for steel structures that are larger, more sophisticated and engineered for greater performance. This facility strengthens our ability to participate in that opportunity with enhanced manufacturing depth and a broader portfolio of capabilities.
Our focus is not simply on adding capacity, but on building the technological and execution capabilities required to support the next generation of industrial and infrastructure projects."

Gautam Suri, Whole-Time Director, Interarch Building Solutions Ltd, said, “Attivaram represents a significant advancement in our heavy structural steel manufacturing capabilities. The facility brings together advanced machinery, precision fabrication and specialised manufacturing processes to address structural requirements that demand a high degree of engineering accuracy and execution excellence.

From heavy structural members to complex assemblies, our objective is to deliver consistent quality at scale while meeting the increasingly demanding specifications of modern construction. This capability will enable us
to take on more complex projects and translate innovative structural designs into efficiently manufactured, high-quality steel solutions."
Shares of Interarch Building Solutions Ltd ended at ₹1,681.00, down by ₹11.05, or 0.65%, on the BSE.

title: Interarch Building Solutions inaugurates Andhra Pradesh heavy steel plant with 24,000 MT capacity
